text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince emphasises "total development" in the Jordan Valley area during a visit to the region, also discusses the optimal use of water and manpower.
- After a five day stoppage, an accord is reached to end electricity workers strike and set up an arbitration councils to resolve the pay dispute.
- Deputy Prime Minister says a cabinet reshuffle possible next April and coming government will not include deputies.
- Organisers of Israeli trade fair continue the preparations for setting up the first exhibition of Israeli industry in Jordan.
- Contacts underway between Israel and Jordan to release Jordanian detainees in Israeli prisons.
- Parliament to discuss on Wednesday the resignation of deputy Nazih Amareen.
- 235 million dinars ($332 million) of road projects earmarked for construction in the kingdom for the next five years.
- End of electricity workers strike, and deputy prime minister emphasises "the need for all to respect the rule of law."
- Head of central tenders committee says violations in the millions of dinars in the construction sector by private companies undertaking work in breach of regulations.
- Justice Minister says the lists of detainees to be pardoned will be announced this week.
- Prime Minister Kabariti begins visit to Spain.
- Informal meeting on refugees opens in Petra with participation of delegates from Jordan, Palestine, Egypt, Israel, the U.S. and Canada.
